text:
ana.peopleops: Quick Q from a teammate in Berlin: dinner on day 1 was €92. They used company card but the receipt only shows total (no itemization) and tip was cash (€10). How do we handle per-diem vs actual receipts when travel is in EUR? Also bank converted the card charge to USD differently than the receipt amount.

omar.finance: Two parts here. 1) Per-diem vs receipts: if you submit actual meal receipts, use those instead of per-diem. For group meals, include attendee names and split amounts. 2) Currency conversion: finance uses the settled card charge in USD for reimbursement matching the bank posting. If the merchant posted in EUR and your bank converted it to USD at a different rate, we reimburse based on the settled USD amount on your statement.

lucas.engineer: For the non-itemized receipt, I can ask vendor for a detailed folio but that might be slow. Is a photo of the physical receipt plus the card statement okay?

omar.finance: Yes, if merchant cannot provide itemization, submit the full merchant receipt + card statement showing the USD settled amount + short note explaining cash tip ("cash tip €10 to waiter, attendees: A,B") and we'll accept. For per-diem: if you choose per-diem instead of receipts, declare per-diem option on report and don't attach meal receipts; pick one method.

ana.peopleops: small policy note: when travel currency != home currency, always include the settled USD charge or conversion rate screenshot from your bank. This avoids variability during reconciliation.

lucas.engineer: Got it. Attendee list: me, sara, and tonia. I'll upload receipt photo + bank posting screenshot and add note about €10 cash tip. Thanks.
